Hi Samantha / Mark — great to see you both on the demo this afternoon. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can align on performance and SLA language before we draft an MoU.

Key asks from your side (from the call):
- Target latency/quality expectations for the real-time assistant flows (you mentioned “near instantaneous” — we need numeric targets)
- Expected concurrency (concurrent active sessions) and peak throughput patterns (bursty vs steady)
- Streaming behavior: do you require partial tokens/events or only complete-message delivery?
- Reporting cadence and what constitutes an SLA breach (P95/P99 windows, measurement method)

What we need from you to move forward:
1) Confirm target SLO numbers you want prioritized (suggest you put P50/P90/P99 targets for a typical 512-token completion and for streaming scenarios).
2) Confirm whether SLAs should be measured end-to-end (HealthLytics client -> Redwood -> client) or service-side (ingress to final token emitted).
3) Any specific exclusions you need (e.g., scheduled maintenance windows, autoscaling warm-up, third-party cloud outages).

Next steps from our side: we will propose concrete SLO measurement language and a remedies matrix (service credit tiers) based on the targets you confirm. I attached the mutual action plan we discussed and a short demo recording link in the MAP.

Thanks Jasmine — good demo. A few clarifications from our side: we care about both interactive web UI latency and server-to-server API latencies for batch jobs. High level targets we discussed internally:

- Interactive assistant (web UI / streaming): P90 <= 250ms, P99 <= 800ms for 512-token sessions. Low token latencies are important for perceived interactivity.
- API (non-streaming batch calls): throughput of ~2k completions/hour at peak; sustained throughput ~300 reqs/min; concurrency ~100 concurrent sessions expected.
- Streaming: we need chunked, incremental token delivery (we use transcripts and progressive UI rendering).

On measurement methodology: we expect the SLA to measure service-side generation time (from Redwood ingress to final token delivered to Redwood’s egress), not including customer network jitter. However we also want a way to capture end-to-end experience in ops dashboards.

Exclusions: we want a 30-minute window for any planned maintenance affecting production and a 10-minute warm-up exclusion for autoscaling events. Any cloud provider-wide outage should be an exclusion.

I attached a short SLO requirements workbook with examples. Please include draft language for remedies and reporting cadence in the next doc.

Attachments: [Attachment: healthlytics_slo_requirements.xlsx]

—Sam

Jasmine — quick technical note based on Sam’s asks:

1) Measurement definition: Redwood currently records request lifecycle timestamps at the gateway ingress and when the runtime emits final token(s). Our default reported latency is "inference+serving" time (ingress -> final token emitted). That aligns with their "service-side generation time" ask. Caveat: if customers use multi-hop proxies or custom edge routing, end-to-end will differ; we can add a client-side ping as a separate metric.

2) Streaming: we support chunked token delivery over HTTP chunked/SSE and gRPC streaming. For UI perceived latency, we recommend measuring time-to-first-token (TTFT) and time-to-last-token (TTLT) as separate SLOs. For their numbers, use TTFT P90 <= 120ms, TTLT P90 <= 250ms for 512 tokens as an internal benchmark — but Sam already proposed P90 250ms which likely corresponds to TTLT.

3) Concurrency/Throughput: 100 concurrent sessions with bursts to 150 should be fine on Dedicated pools with appropriate autoscaling; for Hosted we'd recommend a reserved capacity plan for predictable P99. We'll propose a capacity profile in the MAP.

4) Exclusions: We typically allow planned maintenance windows (up to 60 mins monthly) and short autoscaling warm-up periods (we can accept 10 minutes for measurable scaling events). Cloud provider outages are standard exclusions. We should explicitly call out latency measurement during "fallback to CPU or smaller model" scenarios (those should be excluded from latency SLOs or carry different thresholds).

5) Reporting cadence: recommend weekly latency/availability digest for the first 90 days, then monthly SLA reporting. Also propose automated alerting for any P99 breach above threshold for >1 hour.

I attached a short proposal on measurement options.

Sam / Mark — thanks for the fast replies and for the workbook. Based on your targets and Ben’s notes, please find a concise SLO proposal below for review. If this looks good we’ll include it in the MoU draft and create the first monthly report template.

Proposed SLO language (summary):
- Measurement point: service-side generation time measured at Redwood ingress to final token emitted to Redwood egress (server-side). This excludes customer network egress and client rendering time.
- Streaming flows (interactive UI): measure both time-to-first-token (TTFT) and time-to-last-token (TTLT). Suggested targets: TTFT P90 <= 120ms; TTLT P90 <= 250ms; TTLT P99 <= 800ms for 512-token sessions.
- Non-streaming (batch API): per-completion TTL P95 <= 400ms; throughput sustained 300 reqs/min; peak hourly throughput ~2k completions.
- Concurrency: SLO plan assumes up to 100 concurrent sessions; support for bursts to 150 with Dedicated capacity (recommended).
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (up to 30 minutes per event), autoscaling warm-up (10 minutes per significant scale event), cloud provider outages and force majeure. Any fallback to smaller model or CPU-only execution will trigger alternate SLOs and be documented in the report.
- Reporting cadence & remedies: weekly operational digest for first 90 days, monthly SLA report thereafter with P50/P90/P95/P99 histograms. Remedies: service credit tiers tied to monthly compliance (e.g., 5% credit for single-month P99 breaches exceeding X hours; escalation to enterprise SLA team for repeated breaches). Exact credit brackets to be included in the MoU appendix.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood_slo_proposal_v1.pdf]

Can you confirm the numbers above (specifically the TTFT/TTLT interpretation) and whether the exclusions look acceptable? Once you confirm we’ll get Legal to prepare MoU language and include the remedies matrix.
